To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have produced a panel of monoclals against rat myogeniin, and we have used these antibodies to define epitopes outside of the HLH region where binding interferes either with protein-protein or protein-DNA interactions.

we have developed a panel (seven) of monoclonal antimyogenic antibodies that recognize distinct epitopes outside the HLH domain, that four of these antibodies inhibit the DNA-binding of myogenin heteromeric complexes, and that three of these antibodies inhibit myogenin/E protein heterodimer formation.

the binding of monoclonal anti-myogenin antibodies to epitopes outside the HLH domain interferes with myogenin binding to E-proteins and DNA, suggesting that the bHLH domains of these proteins are not sufficient for their interaction with DNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of a panel of monocloals against rat myogeniin and the mapping of the epitopes recognized by these monoclonals.
the development of a panel of antibodies against myogenin and the use of these to investigate myogenic regulatory protein structure, function and interactions with other regulatory proteins.
the production of monoclonal anti-myogenin antibodies, and their use to map epitopes and study the structure-function relationships of this regulatory protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of antibodies against epitopes on the surface of myogenin outside the HLH domain affects both myogenin/E protein heterodimer and myogenin/E-DNA interactions.
the binding of antibodies to epitopes in the bHLH dimerization domains of the myogenin molecule does not affect DNA binding.

the binding of these antibodies to myogenin outside the HLH domain interferes with the binding of this protein to DNA, and that some, but not all, of these epitopes lie on surfaces that interact with E12.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the myogenin epitopes are located in a number of different regions of the molecule outside the bHLh domain, and that some of these epitopes contribute to the formation of the myogenin-E-protein complex.
myogenin antibodies can interfere with the myogenin/DNA and myogenin/E protein interactions and that these interactions can be mapped by immunopreciptation of myogenin mutants.
the binding of antibodies to epitopes outside the dimerization domain of myogenin can interfere with the interactions of myogenin with both DNA and E-proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
monoclonal antibodies can be used to probe the structure and function of bHLH proteins.
antibodies to epitopes outside the HLH domain may be useful for the study of myogenin function.
the binding of antibodies to epitopes outside the HLH domain can have profound effects on protein-protein and DNA interactions.
